texts.title: De Bello Civili
texts.subtitle: The Civil War
texts.author: Caesar
texts.description: Caesar's account of his war with Pompey and the Senate (49–48 BC), from the Rubicon to Pharsalus.

texts.title: De Bello Gallico
texts.subtitle: The Gallic War
texts.author: Caesar
texts.description: Caesar's own account of his conquest of Gaul (58–50 BC), from the Helvetii to Vercingetorix at Alesia.

texts.title: Carmina
texts.subtitle: Poems (complete)
texts.author: Catullus
texts.description: All of Catullus' poems: love and hate for Lesbia, friends and enemies, myth and invective. Some are sexually explicit.

texts.title: Ad Familiares
texts.subtitle: Letters to Friends
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's letters to friends, family and colleagues — Caesar, Pompey, Cato, Tiro — over twenty years.

texts.title: Ad Quintum Fratrem
texts.subtitle: Letters to his Brother Quintus
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's letters to his younger brother, including advice on governing the province of Asia.

texts.title: De Amicitia
texts.subtitle: On Friendship (Laelius)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A dialogue on friendship, set just after the death of Scipio and voiced by his friend Laelius (44 BC).

texts.title: De Imperio Cn. Pompei
texts.subtitle: On Pompey's Command (Pro Lege Manilia)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's first political speech (66 BC), urging that Pompey be given command against Mithridates.

texts.title: De Officiis
texts.subtitle: On Duties
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's last philosophical work, written for his son: what is right, what is useful, and when they conflict.

texts.title: In Catilinam
texts.subtitle: Against Catiline (Speeches I–IV)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's four speeches of 63 BC exposing Catiline's conspiracy against the Republic.

texts.title: In Verrem
texts.subtitle: Against Verres
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's prosecution of Verres, governor of Sicily, for extortion (70 BC).

texts.title: Philippics
texts.subtitle: Against Mark Antony (Speeches I–XIV)
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's fourteen speeches against Mark Antony (44–43 BC), the last fight for the Republic.

texts.title: Pro Archia
texts.subtitle: In Defence of the Poet Archias
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A short, celebrated speech defending the poet Archias's citizenship, and the value of literature itself (62 BC).

texts.title: Pro Cluentio
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Aulus Cluentius
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's longest surviving defence speech: a murder trial full of family poisonings and bribed juries (66 BC).

texts.title: Pro Ligario
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Ligarius
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A plea before Caesar himself for the Pompeian Ligarius (46 BC).

texts.title: Pro Marcello
texts.subtitle: On the Pardon of Marcellus
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero thanks Caesar for pardoning his old enemy Marcellus (46 BC): praise with an edge.

texts.title: Pro Milone
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Milo
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's defence of Milo for the killing of Clodius on the Appian Way (52 BC), in the version he published.

texts.title: Pro Murena
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Murena
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: A witty defence of the consul-elect Murena on a bribery charge, in the middle of the Catilinarian crisis (63 BC).

texts.title: Pro Rege Deiotaro
texts.subtitle: In Defence of King Deiotarus
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero defends the Galatian king Deiotarus, accused of plotting to murder Caesar (45 BC).

texts.title: Pro Roscio Amerino
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Sextus Roscius of Ameria
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's first great criminal case (80 BC): a son accused of parricide, and Sulla's freedman behind it.

texts.title: Pro Sestio
texts.subtitle: In Defence of Sestius
texts.author: Cicero
texts.description: Cicero's defence of Sestius, and his manifesto for the 'best men' of the Republic (56 BC).

texts.title: Ars Poetica
texts.subtitle: The Art of Poetry
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Horace's verse letter on writing poetry and drama, hugely influential on later criticism.

texts.title: Epistles
texts.subtitle: Epistulae, Books I–II
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Verse letters to friends and patrons on philosophy, ambition and how to live.

texts.title: Odes
texts.subtitle: Carmina, Books I–IV
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Horace's lyric poems: carpe diem, friendship, wine, love and the brevity of life.

texts.title: Satires
texts.subtitle: Sermones, Books I–II
texts.author: Horace
texts.description: Horace's conversational satires: the bore on the Sacred Way, the town and country mouse.

texts.title: Satires
texts.subtitle: Saturae 1–16
texts.author: Juvenal
texts.description: Juvenal's furious satires on Rome: the city's dangers, women, the vanity of human wishes. Some explicit content.

texts.title: De Mortibus Persecutorum
texts.subtitle: On the Deaths of the Persecutors
texts.author: Lactantius
texts.description: Lactantius' account of the Great Persecution under Diocletian and the grim ends of the emperors who persecuted Christians, down to Constantine (c. AD 315).

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 1
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 1
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: The founding of Rome and the regal period, from Aeneas to the expulsion of Tarquin.

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 2
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 2
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: The early Republic: Horatius at the bridge, Coriolanus, the secession of the plebs.

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 21
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 21
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: The outbreak of the Second Punic War: Saguntum, and Hannibal's crossing of the Alps.

texts.title: Ab Urbe Condita 22
texts.subtitle: History of Rome, Book 22
texts.author: Livy
texts.description: Hannibal in Italy: Lake Trasimene, Fabius the Delayer, and the disaster at Cannae.

texts.title: Amores
texts.subtitle: Love Poems, Books I–III
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's first collection: witty love elegies to Corinna. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Ars Amatoria
texts.subtitle: The Art of Love, Books I–III
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's mock-didactic guide to seduction, the poem that helped get him exiled. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Epistulae ex Ponto
texts.subtitle: Letters from the Black Sea, Books I–IV
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's later letters from exile in Tomis, addressed by name to friends in Rome.

texts.title: Fasti
texts.subtitle: The Roman Calendar, Books I–VI
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's poem on the Roman calendar, January to June: festivals, myths and stars, day by day.

texts.title: Heroides
texts.subtitle: Letters of the Heroines
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Verse letters from mythical women to the men who left them: Penelope, Dido, Medea, Ariadne.

texts.title: Metamorphoses
texts.subtitle: Transformations, Books I–XV
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Ovid's epic of transformations, from Chaos to the deification of Caesar: Apollo and Daphne, Narcissus, Pyramus and Thisbe. (Kline's translation is in prose.)

texts.title: Remedia Amoris
texts.subtitle: Cures for Love
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: The sequel to the Ars Amatoria: how to fall out of love.

texts.title: Tristia
texts.subtitle: Sorrows, Books I–V
texts.author: Ovid
texts.description: Poems from exile on the Black Sea: the journey, the last night in Rome, and pleas for recall.

texts.title: Satyricon
texts.subtitle: Including the Cena Trimalchionis
texts.author: Petronius
texts.description: The surviving fragments of Petronius' comic novel, including Trimalchio's dinner party. Some explicit content.

texts.title: Fabulae
texts.subtitle: Fables (Books I–V and Appendix)
texts.author: Phaedrus
texts.description: Aesop's fables in Latin verse: the wolf and the lamb, the fox and the grapes. Short and simple, ideal for beginners.

texts.title: Epistulae
texts.subtitle: Letters, Books I–X
texts.author: Pliny the Younger
texts.description: Pliny's letters: Vesuvius and his uncle's death, a haunted house, his villas, and his correspondence with Trajan on the Christians.

texts.title: Elegies
texts.subtitle: Elegiae, Books I–IV
texts.author: Propertius
texts.description: Love elegies for Cynthia, and in Book IV, poems on Rome's origins. (Kline's translation is in prose.)

texts.title: Bellum Catilinae
texts.subtitle: The Conspiracy of Catiline
texts.author: Sallust
texts.description: Sallust's history of Catiline's conspiracy: the other side of Cicero's In Catilinam, with the speeches of Caesar and Cato.

texts.title: Bellum Iugurthinum
texts.subtitle: The Jugurthine War
texts.author: Sallust
texts.description: Sallust's account of Rome's war with the Numidian king Jugurtha, and the corruption it exposed at home.

texts.title: Caligula
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 4: Caligula
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Caligula: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Augustus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 2: Augustus
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Augustus: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Claudius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 5: Claudius
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Claudius: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Iulius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 1: Julius Caesar
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Julius Caesar: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Titus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 11: Titus
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Titus: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Divus Vespasianus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 10: Vespasian
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Vespasian: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Domitianus
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 12: Domitian
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Domitian: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Galba
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 7: Galba
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Galba: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Nero
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 6: Nero
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Nero: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Otho
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 8: Otho
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Otho: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Tiberius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 3: Tiberius
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Tiberius: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Vitellius
texts.subtitle: Lives of the Caesars 9: Vitellius
texts.author: Suetonius
texts.description: Suetonius' life of Vitellius: career, character, habits and gossip.

texts.title: Agricola
texts.subtitle: The Life of Agricola
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Tacitus' life of his father-in-law, the governor who completed the conquest of Britain.

texts.title: Annals
texts.subtitle: From the Death of Augustus
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Rome under Tiberius, Claudius and Nero, in Tacitus' surviving books (1–6, 11–16).

texts.title: Germania
texts.subtitle: On the Origin and Situation of the Germans
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Tacitus' ethnography of the Germanic peoples beyond the Rhine.

texts.title: Histories
texts.subtitle: The Year of the Four Emperors (Books I–V)
texts.author: Tacitus
texts.description: Civil war after Nero's death: Galba, Otho, Vitellius and the rise of Vespasian (AD 69–70).

texts.title: Elegies
texts.subtitle: Books I–III, with Lygdamus and Sulpicia
texts.author: Tibullus
texts.description: Love elegies for Delia and Nemesis, and the poems of Sulpicia, the only female Roman poet whose work survives.

texts.title: Aeneid
texts.subtitle: The Aeneid (Books I–XII)
texts.author: Virgil
texts.description: Virgil's epic of Aeneas, from the fall of Troy to the founding of the Roman people.

texts.title: Eclogues
texts.subtitle: Bucolics
texts.author: Virgil
texts.description: Ten pastoral poems of shepherds, song contests and lost land, including the 'messianic' Fourth Eclogue.

texts.title: Georgics
texts.subtitle: Books I–IV
texts.author: Virgil
texts.description: Virgil's poem on farming, trees, livestock and bees, ending with Orpheus and Eurydice.
